events.title: An earthquake destroys large parts of the Walls of Constantinople
events.description: A powerful earthquake destroyed large parts of the Walls of Constantinople, including 57 towers. With Attila the Hun threatening from the Balkans, Theodosius II had them restored, reportedly in a record 60 days, using the city's chariot-racing factions.

events.title: Otto I convenes a synod in Rome to depose Pope John XII
events.description: Under the authority of Emperor Otto I, a possibly uncanonical synod met in Saint Peter's Basilica to depose Pope John XII, who had crowned Otto emperor in 962, for armed rebellion against him. The synod sat until 4 December.
events.html: Under the authority of Emperor Otto I, a possibly uncanonical synod met in Saint Peter's Basilica to depose Pope John XII, who had crowned Otto emperor in 962, for armed rebellion against him. The synod sat until 4 December.

events.title: Henry III issues the Charter of the Forest
events.description: The young King Henry III, under the regency of William Marshal, 1st Earl of Pembroke, issued the Charter of the Forest at Old St Paul's Cathedral, restoring free men's rights of access to the royal forest. It complemented Magna Carta.
events.html: The young King Henry III, under the regency of William Marshal, 1st Earl of Pembroke, issued the Charter of the Forest at Old St Paul's Cathedral, restoring free men's rights of access to the royal forest. It complemented Magna Carta.

events.title: Abraham Lincoln is elected president
events.description: Abraham Lincoln won the presidency with under 40 per cent of the popular vote, carrying only northern states. His victory prompted South Carolina to secede within weeks, followed by six more states.
events.html: Abraham Lincoln won the presidency with under 40 per cent of the popular vote, carrying only northern states. His victory prompted South Carolina to secede within weeks, followed by six more states.

events.title: Rutgers and Princeton play the first college football game
events.description: Rutgers beat Princeton 6-4 in New Brunswick, New Jersey, in the first intercollegiate football match. The rules resembled soccer more than modern American football.
events.html: Rutgers beat Princeton 6-4 in New Brunswick, New Jersey, in the first intercollegiate football match. The rules resembled soccer more than modern American football.

events.title: Gandhi is arrested leading a march of Indian miners
events.description: In South Africa, Gandhi was arrested at Palmford while leading over 2,000 striking Indian workers across the Transvaal border in defiance of discriminatory laws. The campaign won concessions in 1914.
events.html: In South Africa, Gandhi was arrested at Palmford while leading over 2,000 striking Indian workers across the Transvaal border in defiance of discriminatory laws. The campaign won concessions in 1914.

events.title: Canadian troops capture Passchendaele
events.description: Canadian forces took the ruined village of Passchendaele, ending the Third Battle of Ypres. The British-led offensive had gained a few miles of Flemish mud at a cost of hundreds of thousands of casualties.
events.html: Canadian forces took the ruined village of Passchendaele, ending the Third Battle of Ypres. The British-led offensive had gained a few miles of Flemish mud at a cost of hundreds of thousands of casualties.

events.title: The UN General Assembly calls for sanctions on South Africa
events.description: Resolution 1761 condemned apartheid and urged member states to break diplomatic ties and boycott South African trade. It also set up a special committee against apartheid.
